resolves.action_name: Use a balanced setup (same number of traces per plaintext value) and implement shuffling of batches.
resolves.cause_name: Unbalanced plaintext distribution leads to biased leakage estimates, which can affect collision detection.
resolves.source_text: This balanced setup allows to remove the bias of the plaintext distribution and it can be easily implemented using shuffling of batches.

resolves.action_name: Use the scalar product distinguisher (D_sto.coll.bal).
resolves.cause_name: For Gaussian distributed leakage function values, the scalar product distinguisher (D_sto.coll.bal) is optimal in the maximum likelihood sense.
resolves.source_text: Remarkably, this special result is independent of the parameters... It also shows the optimality in terms of maximum likelihood of the D_sto.coll.bal distinguisher in case of Gaussian distributed leakage function values.

resolves.action_name: Switch to Shortest Distance First (SDF) extractor for noise minimization
resolves.cause_name: Existing extractors (TAILS) only maximize variance of data-dependent component and ignore noise component, resulting in limited SNR improvement
resolves.source_text: Existing extractors only maximize the variance of data-dependent power consumption component and ignore the noise component, which results in very limited SNR to improve.

resolves.action_name: Switch to Mean optimized MESF (MMESF) extractor for mean-based estimation
resolves.cause_name: Directly using single noisy samples to estimate data-dependent component introduces significant estimation error
resolves.source_text: It is not very good to directly exploit l_i(τ) containing noise to estimate data-dependent power consumption, which will introduce significant but unnecessary estimation error.

resolves.action_name: Add trace extraction step to pipeline for complexity reduction
resolves.cause_name: When attacker has enough traces to guarantee successful attacks, goal shifts from increasing success rate to lowering computational complexity
resolves.source_text: We only consider the case that the number of power traces owned by the attacker is sufficient to guarantee his successful attacks, and the goal of his extraction is to lower the complexity rather than increase the success rate.

resolves.action_name: Use a non-injective leakage function that incurs information loss (e.g., Hamming weight, LSB, MSB).
resolves.cause_name: Using an injective leakage function loses no information about the intermediate value, making all keys equally likely under the mutual information metric.
resolves.source_text: Theorem 1 states that DDLA with an injective leakage function cannot distinguish the correct key and any wrong key at all.

resolves.action_name: Choose leakage function based on prior knowledge of device leakage characteristics (e.g., typical functions like Hamming weight, LSB, MSB).
resolves.cause_name: No method exists to simultaneously estimate the correct key and the optimal leakage function without prior knowledge.
resolves.source_text: DDLA essentially requires some knowledge or assumption on leakage characteristics to determine an appropriate g.

resolves.action_name: Use likelihood-based distinguisher (product of probabilities) as defined in Equation (7).
resolves.cause_name: The sum-of-probabilities distinguisher used in the original collision DL-SCA is not optimal.
resolves.source_text: our distinguisher achieved the SR for a given number of traces, which was almost the same as that of the TA, ... our distinguisher and TA achieve higher performance than the Staib-Moradi collision DL-SCA.

resolves.action_name: Use a dedicated architecture with a shared feature extractor across all bytes and separate classifiers per byte.
resolves.cause_name: Training separate neural network per byte limits the amount of training data available for each model.
resolves.source_text: the proposed NN architecture shares the same feature extractor for inference of the plaintext/ciphertext information of all bytes. This allows feature extractor training to be performed using 16 times more traces.

resolves.action_name: Prefer collision DL-SCA over DDLA when leakage function is unknown.
resolves.cause_name: The appropriate leakage function is device-dependent and cannot be determined without knowing the correct key.
resolves.source_text: the performance of the DDLAs heavily depends on the leakage function ( i.e. , LSB or MSB herein). ... This indicates the instability of DDLA as a non-profiled SCA.

resolves.action_name: Check that selection function is bijective (or has bijective redundant form) and satisfies Assumption 1 (KIC). Also verify that leakages for each Sbox are independent and separable.
resolves.cause_name: Selection function is not bijective (or does not satisfy KIC) or side-channel leakages are not i.i.d. and separable in time domain.
resolves.source_text: The applicability of the collision DL-SCA depends on the following two conditions: ...

resolves.action_name: Choose S-box output as intermediate value for CPA or machine learning attacks
resolves.cause_name: Non-linear operations (e.g., S-box) have stronger power consumption leakage than linear transformations
resolves.source_text: the S-box is a non-linear transformation that generates significant power consumption during the transformation, as compared to linear transformations. Therefore, choosing this point as an intermediate value for power analysis attacks makes it easier to break the key.

resolves.action_name: Apply PCA for dimensionality reduction before training
resolves.cause_name: High-dimensional raw trace data leads to excessive computational complexity and training time
resolves.source_text: The original power traces consist of 24,400 sampling points. Regardless of the training mode, a dataset with 24,400 dimensions would require an impractically long training time. ... PCA reduces a set of potentially correlated high-dimensional variables into a set of lower-dimensional, linearly uncorrelated variables known as principal components.

resolves.action_name: Select continuous window of 6000 samples with highest correlation
resolves.cause_name: Excessive noise and irrelevant samples in the full trace dilute the relevant leakage signal, and temporal characteristics are important for model learning
resolves.source_text: every 8-byte key is related to approximately 6000 sample points in the power trace. ... To preserve the temporal characteristics, we selected a continuous window of 6000 sample points with the highest correlation coefficient.

resolves.action_name: examine register usage and data flow to identify sensitive intermediate values
resolves.cause_name: Leakage corresponds to instructions processing intermediate values (e.g., S-box output) that are impacted by a changed plaintext byte.
resolves.source_text: The cause of these leakages can be understood by observing the contents of a2 and a4 registers at these instructions... a2 stores a value that is impacted by a change in PT5, thus explaining the TVLA leaks.

resolves.action_name: avoid reusing the same architectural register for different masked bytes in ShiftRows
resolves.cause_name: Register reuse in ShiftRows operation leads to mask cancellation: loading a new masked byte into a register that still holds a previous masked byte (with the same mask) effectively removes the mask, leaking Hamming distance.
resolves.source_text: When loading byte s_m9 in the register containing s_m5, the effect... removes the mask. As a result, the code will leak HD(s5, s9)...

resolves.action_name: use fixed-vs-fixed TVLA mode for root-cause analysis
resolves.cause_name: Fixed-vs-random TVLA only indicates leakage presence; fixed-vs-fixed TVLA (varying one or a few plaintext bytes) isolates leakage to specific intermediate values.
resolves.source_text: Fixed-vs-Fixed: This mode compares traces where only one or more plaintext bytes vary, enabling detailed root-cause analysis.

resolves.action_name: Run multiple independent trials (e.g., different random seeds, trace subsets) and report variability (mean ± std or confidence intervals), not just best-case results.
resolves.cause_name: Stochastic factors in training (for DL) or trace selection during evaluation (for non-profiled SCA) introduce significant variance; reporting only a single run does not reflect typical performance.
resolves.source_text: Statistics: Avoid 'best run only'; report variability (e.g., over seeds/splits and/or evaluation sampling) and specify what error bars summarize.

resolves.action_name: Release training and attack scripts (or equivalent pseudocode), including commands to reproduce key tables/figures, and specify the software environment.
resolves.cause_name: Lack of accessible code, data, or precise preprocessing documentation prevents independent verification and comparison.
resolves.source_text: Code: Release training + attack scripts (or equivalent pseudocode if release is impossible), including GE computation script; include commands to reproduce key tables/figures; specify the software environment.

resolves.action_name: Document the exact preprocessing pipeline (alignment/filtering/windowing/normalization) used to produce the traces/features in experiments.
resolves.cause_name: Preprocessing steps (alignment, filtering, windowing, normalization) are often not fully documented, making it impossible to recreate the exact input traces.
resolves.source_text: Data: ... document the exact preprocessing pipeline (alignment/filtering/windowing/normalization) used to produce the traces/features in experiments.

resolves.action_name: Use one distinguisher for all tests; avoid exhaustive testing of multiple distinguishers
resolves.cause_name: Different statistical distinguishers are equivalent under same leakage model for standard DPA scenarios
resolves.source_text: testing does not always require to investigate all distinguishers exhaustively: it is sometimes sound to use 'one distinguisher for all'.

resolves.action_name: Focus on selecting or profiling an accurate leakage model rather than optimizing statistical test
resolves.cause_name: Leakage model selection has greater impact on success rate than statistical tool choice
resolves.source_text: the selection of a leakage model has more impact on the success rate than the selection of the statistical tool to exploit this model.

resolves.action_name: Add analog carrier suppression circuit before ADC
resolves.cause_name: Carrier wave dominates ADC, saturating it and reducing effective bits for side-channel information
resolves.source_text: developed analog circuit ... capable of delaying and scaling the sine wave of the crystal, in order to match its amplitude and phase to that of the EM measurements, before subtracting the pure sine from the EM measurements.

resolves.action_name: Align only specific region of interest instead of entire trace
resolves.cause_name: Asynchronous device operation causes timing variations outside region of interest
resolves.source_text: the analyzed smartcard performs the operations in an asynchronous manner ... The alignment has thus to be performed with respect to the part of the trace we aim to examine

resolves.action_name: Switch to binwise CPA method
resolves.cause_name: Timing jitter from asynchronous operation and dummy cycles misaligns leakage points
resolves.source_text: extract local maxima and minima ... grouped on the basis of their time coordinate by dividing the time axis into equal intervals or bins ... The CPA is performed binwise

resolves.action_name: Experimentally determine digital filter cutoff frequencies
resolves.cause_name: Optimal filter cutoffs are device-dependent and require experimental determination
resolves.source_text: Good values for the filter cutoff frequencies f_lowpass and f_highpass were determined experimentally

resolves.action_name: extract peaks (amplitudes) and use them for alignment
resolves.cause_name: Data-dependent leakage occurs at clock edges, but jitter misaligns traces.
resolves.source_text: Another problem is that all of the target devices are clocked by a noisy internal oscillator. Hence we had to find a way to remove the clock jitter. ... we extract the peaks from the power consumption in software, and base our DPA attack solely on the amplitudes of the peaks.

resolves.action_name: choose an intermediate value that depends on known data, key bits, is easy to predict, and has high nonlinearity
resolves.cause_name: To avoid ghost peaks and have a strong DPA, choose an intermediate value with high nonlinearity with respect to the key.
resolves.source_text: Furthermore, it is advisable to choose a value that has a high degree of nonlinearity with respect to the key, to avoid so-called 'ghost peaks' for 'similar' keys.

resolves.action_name: use Hamming distance of the state register as power model
resolves.cause_name: The combinational part leakage is small, key register has constant power (due to rotation), so focus on state register.
resolves.source_text: Hence, we focus on the state register y. We execute a correlation DPA attack (CPA) [2] based on the following hypothetical power model ...

resolves.action_name: adjust sampling rate and trace count accordingly
resolves.cause_name: DIP packages have higher SNR than SOIC, and lower sampling rates require more traces.
resolves.source_text: In the best case we were able to recover the secret key of DIP package ICs from only six power traces when sampling at a rate of 200 MS/s. At most 30 power traces are sufficient ... even with low-cost equipment, e.g., an oscilloscope with a maximum sample rate as low as 50MS/s enables finding the secret key from only 60 power traces.

resolves.action_name: consider using EM near field probe as a non-invasive alternative
resolves.cause_name: EM near field probe can capture the same leakage as power consumption, with similar SNR.
resolves.source_text: Contrary to our assumption that the SNR would suffer from environmental noise ... the results obtained and the number of traces needed are very comparable to the case of power traces

resolves.action_name: acquire more traces to compensate
resolves.cause_name: Data-dependent execution time leads to increasing misalignment over rounds.
resolves.source_text: While performing the attack we noticed that the correlation coefficient of the correct key become continuously worse with an increasing number of rounds. ... This gradual decrease of the correlation is due to a misalignment that occurs during the execution of the KeeLoq algorithm.

resolves.action_name: Use Sum of Absolute Differences (SAD) trigger for pattern matching
resolves.cause_name: In real-world targets, an IO line indicating encryption/decryption activity is often not exposed, making synchronization difficult.
resolves.source_text: Typical work demonstrating side-channel attacks uses an IO line of the microcontroller that indicates when the encryption (or decryption) routine is running. This provides an attacker with a perfectly synchronized trigger event, but in real implementations this will not be available. For this work the Sum of Absolute Differences (SAD) trigger built into the ChipWhisperer is used.

resolves.action_name: Apply SAD resynchronization for later rounds
resolves.cause_name: The AES-256 implementation has non-constant execution time, causing later rounds to drift.
resolves.source_text: Traces may also need to be synchronized in time. In particular the AES-256 implementation used here has nonconstant execution time... To compensate for this a SAD resynchronization element is used during analysis for the 13th round.

resolves.action_name: Switch to attacking transformed key Y13
resolves.cause_name: The MixColumns inverse operation in round 13 mixes bytes, making a single-byte guess impossible if attacking the state directly.
resolves.source_text: We can however take advantage of the linearity of the Mix^{-1}(a) operation to rearrange (2)... Once we fully determine Y13, we can use (8) to determine the desired encryption key for round 13, K13.

resolves.action_name: Verify attack feasibility and consider alternatives
resolves.cause_name: The IV is applied via a linear XOR operation. A single-bit change in the IV guess causes a single-bit change in the hypothetical leakage (Hamming Weight), leading to high correlation for guesses with similar bit patterns. Additionally, the bitwise inverse of the correct guess produces the same absolute correlation (opposite sign), confusing ranking.
resolves.source_text: The CPA attack never fully recovers the IV even with 5000 traces... Note the wrong guesses have a very close bit pattern to the correct value... the absolute value of the correlation cannot be used.

resolves.action_name: Decrypt firmware file to find signature
resolves.cause_name: The signature is a fixed 4-byte sequence prepended to each plaintext block before encryption. Once the key is recovered, the signature becomes visible in the decrypted data.
resolves.source_text: Provided the attacker has access to an encrypted firmware file, they can simply decrypt this file using the key determined with a CPA attack. The signature will be readily apparent due to the presence of a repeated fixed four-byte sequence in the decrypted file.

resolves.action_name: Use chosen plaintext where only the target byte varies and other bytes are fixed (e.g., 0x00)
resolves.cause_name: Using random plaintext for all bytes does not isolate the target tweak byte, leading to lower correlation peaks and requiring more traces
resolves.source_text: 其中，xx代表为随机数，00代表该字节输入始终保持为固定值00。

resolves.action_name: Use a multi-stage CPA that incorporates multiple consecutive attack points (time samples)
resolves.cause_name: Due to the shifting operation, different hypotheses (e.g., values that are multiples of powers of two) can produce identical Hamming distance values at a single attack point, leading to false positives
resolves.source_text: 当只对一个目标点进行分析时，有多个相关假设值具有相同的汉明值特征...多阶段结合的 CPA 分析方法可以消除数据移位的影响。

resolves.action_name: Use a chosen-plaintext method to constrain the input and reduce the key guess space.
resolves.cause_name: The linear transformation L after the S-boxes mixes the bytes, making the leakage of individual bytes difficult to isolate.
resolves.source_text: 在SM4的轮计算过程中，S盒变换后的4个字节又经历了一次线性的L变换，使得这4个字节充分混淆，难以像传统模型那样利用算法中1个S盒只处理1个字节

resolves.action_name: Use Welch's t-test as the distinguisher instead of, or in conjunction with, correlation.
resolves.cause_name: Welch's t-test provides a statistically sound measure of difference between two sets and allows for incremental computation, which is efficient and interpretable.
resolves.source_text: 本文引入了Welch's t检验的方法来评估在SM4算法的选择明文功耗分析中差分后的两类功耗轨迹集合之间的差异程度，将t值作为对泄露量的衡量

resolves.action_name: Apply PCA as a preprocessing step to reduce the number of points per trace.
resolves.cause_name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) can reduce dimensionality while preserving the most important information, thus reducing computational complexity.
resolves.source_text: 本文引入主成分分析来对原始的功耗轨迹信息进行预处理操作，使得提取出的新轨迹样本拥有更少的样本点，得到更能反映数据相关的旁路泄露信息

resolves.action_name: For attacking the first byte of the round key in SM4 hardware, use a selection function that classifies traces based on the two least significant bits of C0.
resolves.cause_name: Selection function 2 (based on the two least significant bits of the intermediate value C0) provides a finer classification of traces, better utilizing the leakage information.
resolves.source_text: 函数2能够获得更好的攻击效果...使用500条曲线就可以攻击成功，这种选择函数的攻击效果优于前两种的原因，在于它更加细化了对轨迹的分类

resolves.action_name: Use multi-bit DPA
resolves.cause_name: Single-bit DPA may lead to false results and the choice of the bit has direct impact on attack success.
resolves.source_text: Because DPA builds its hypothesis on a single bit value, its assumptions regarding the leakage are very general. This may be one of the reasons for false results, so-called 'ghost peaks'. ... This fact is a motivation for multi-bit DPA

resolves.action_name: Use Spearman correlation coefficient
resolves.cause_name: CPA assumes linear relationship, but the relationship may be monotonic.
resolves.source_text: The CPA attack assumes a linear relationship between the predicted leakage and the physical observation. However, this requirement can be relaxed to monotonicity by using the Spearman coefficient instead of the Pearson coefficient.

resolves.action_name: Avoid using an injective leakage function
resolves.cause_name: If the leakage function is injective, different key guesses yield a permutation of the partitions, making the mutual information constant.
resolves.source_text: The leakage function must be selected so that a different ˆ k must not yield a permutation of ˆ L ˆ k . ... This problem does not only pertain to MIA, but to every partitioning attack.

resolves.action_name: Use convolutional neural network (CNN) in DDLA
resolves.cause_name: Univariate attacks require synchronization, but traces may be desynchronized due to jitter or countermeasures.
resolves.source_text: Translation-invariance property of convolutional networks can be exploited to attack desynchronized traces, whereas previously described attacks would require synchronization of the traces during preprocessing.

resolves.action_name: Use sliding window attack
resolves.cause_name: Hiding in time countermeasures spread the leakage over time.
resolves.source_text: When the leakage is spread in time in a more chaotic manner, e.g., by clock jitter, a sliding window attack may be used, where a finite number of (consecutive or not) time samples is summed/integrated to a single value.

resolves.action_name: Use centered product combining function
resolves.cause_name: Noise amplification in higher-order attacks.
resolves.source_text: Assuming very noisy observations, the centered product combining function leads to a more efficient attack than the absolute difference combining.

resolves.action_name: Use threshold ±4.5 or ±5
resolves.cause_name: Need a threshold to reject null hypothesis with high confidence.
resolves.source_text: In side-channel analysis, the threshold ± 4.5 or ± 5 for the t-value is often considered, which roughly corresponds to significance level a ≤ 10 -5 .

resolves.action_name: Eliminate zero columns
resolves.cause_name: Zero columns increase degrees of freedom without contributing to the test.
resolves.source_text: Columns containing only zeros should be eliminated to decrease number of degrees of freedom.

resolves.action_name: average multiple power traces of the same encryption
resolves.cause_name: uncorrelated noise from voltage source, quantization, or intrinsic noise
resolves.source_text: uncorrelated noise ... can be decreased by averaging power traces of equal encryptions ... we found out that averaging of N=10 power traces was clearly sufficient

resolves.action_name: use additional measurement circuitry to decouple voltage source or acquire at higher sampling rates
resolves.cause_name: external voltage source noise or low sampling rate
resolves.source_text: Averaging may not even be necessary at all if additional measurement circuitry is used in order to decouple the external voltage source from the target hardware or data is acquired at higher sampling rates.

resolves.action_name: interpret as a collision
resolves.cause_name: indicates that the same data was processed (collision)
resolves.source_text: we discovered that a correlation coefficient greater than 95% generally indicated a collision.

resolves.action_name: Use profiled DPA (e.g., Gaussian templates) instead of non-profiled DPA when possible, as it is guaranteed to succeed given enough traces.
resolves.cause_name: Profiled DPA builds templates (e.g., Gaussian, regression-based) that directly model the conditional probability distribution of leakages given the key and plaintext, capturing the true leakage function.
resolves.source_text: Separation: only profiled DPA is guaranteed to succeed against any leaking device (!)

resolves.action_name: Prefer Gaussian template attacks over CPA when a profiling phase is feasible, as they leverage a more accurate leakage model.
resolves.cause_name: Gaussian templates exploit a better (profiled) model of the leakage distribution, whereas CPA relies on a simplified model (e.g., Hamming weight).
resolves.source_text: Gaussian templates outperforms CPA because it (usually) exploits a better (profiled) model

resolves.action_name: To trade data for time, target more than 8 bits at once (e.g., 32 bits in a 32-bit architecture) to cancel part of the algorithmic noise.
resolves.cause_name: Algorithmic noise from non-targeted parallel bits reduces the correlation between the predicted model (for the target bits) and the total leakage.
resolves.source_text: Target more than 8 bits at once. Cancels (a part of) the « algorithmic noise »

resolves.action_name: Switch to dynamic alignment technique
resolves.cause_name: Static alignment cannot handle non-linear misalignment from countermeasures like random delays or clock randomization
resolves.source_text: 当密码模块中主动引入了随机延时或者时钟频率变化时，静态对齐技术无法获得完全对齐的信号，则应使用“动态对齐”技术。

resolves.action_name: apply dynamic alignment
resolves.cause_name: Implementation actively introduces random timing delays or clock frequency variations as a countermeasure, breaking the assumption of fixed operation timing.
resolves.source_text: When the implementation actively introduces random timing delays or clock frequency variations, the static displacement cannot attain the full alignment of the traces. In this case, the so called dynamic alignment is applied.

resolves.action_name: apply noise reduction preprocessing
resolves.cause_name: Noise in side-channel measurements can obscure leakage, requiring preprocessing to improve SNR for reliable statistical testing.
resolves.source_text: A noise reduction shall be performed by the tester calculating the mean of different traces (10 cryptographic executions should be performed for the same inputs set, to get one single trace). For security level 4: filter in frequency (band-pass filter according to the module operation frequency).

resolves.action_name: implement noise reduction measures in setup
resolves.cause_name: Electronic noise from power supply, clock generator, conducted/radiated emissions, and quantisation can obscure the side-channel signal.
resolves.source_text: The power supply should never be powered directly by a PC. The measurement setup should be built with two PCBs: a measurement board and an interface board, isolated by opto- or magnetic couplers. The PCB with the attacked device can be put in a Faraday cage. EM should be preferred for side-channel resistance validation to reduce switching noise.

resolves.action_name: use chosen-input method
resolves.cause_name: Random inputs may not efficiently exercise the specific leakage of interest, requiring many traces to achieve statistical significance.
resolves.source_text: If the tester knows the value of the CSP, the tester can select a set of 'good' texts for leakage analysis with respect to the known CSP. This method can dramatically reduce the necessary number of power/EM traces.

resolves.action_name: Replace univariate tests with the multivariate Hotelling's T²-test, which naturally accounts for dependencies and provides correct false positive control.
resolves.cause_name: Univariate tests (e.g., Welch's t-test) assume independence between trace points, leading to inaccurate p‑values and false positive rates when dependencies exist.
resolves.source_text: Hotelling's T²-test is inherently multivariate and does not require an independence assumption. This allows a stable and fair control of the false positive and false negative.

resolves.action_name: In open‑source settings, use a priori knowledge of the implementation to preselect only the points where data‑dependent leakage is expected, thereby increasing the effective density.
resolves.cause_name: Low density reduces the efficiency of leakage detection because many non‑informative points increase noise and dilute the signal.
resolves.source_text: leakage detection with T²‑test benefits from the open‑source requirement ... it allows to use a priori knowledge of the possible leakage location to increase the density.

resolves.action_name: Compute both the Hypothetical Information (HI) and the Perceived Information (PI) to obtain lower and upper bounds for the true MI.
resolves.cause_name: The true leakage distribution is unknown, so MI cannot be computed directly. Model errors (estimation and assumption errors) can lead to over‑ or under‑estimation of security.
resolves.source_text: the eHI provides an average upper bound that converges monotonically towards the MI, and the ePI provides a lower bound.

resolves.action_name: Use G‑ESASCA (Gaussian Encoding‑only SASCA) which leverages the knowledge of masking randomness and the independent‑shares assumption to build templates per share, reducing the number of templates and speeding up convergence.
resolves.cause_name: Profiling without knowledge of the masking randomness requires estimating mixtures with many components, which converges slowly.
resolves.source_text: the distinguishers that have the lowest profiling (data) complexity are also the ones that take advantage of more assumptions. Concretely, we observe that the G‑ESASCA is the fastest.

resolves.action_name: Dissect the countermeasures by performing sub‑attacks on each component separately: first recover the multiplicative mask, then the permutation seeds, and finally the additive shares.
resolves.cause_name: Combined countermeasures multiply the complexity factors; attacking them as a whole requires summing over all randomness and permutations, which is computationally prohibitive.
resolves.source_text: We use knowledge of the implementation to perform countermeasures' dissection. By dissection, we mean a detailed analysis of each ingredient of a protected implementation, in order to limit their (combined) impact as much as possible.

resolves.action_name: Exploit permutation leakage (e.g., from memory addresses or control flow) to estimate the shuffling order, thereby reducing the number of indexes that need to be summed over.
resolves.cause_name: Shuffling increases attack complexity by forcing the adversary to sum over all possible permutation indexes. However, the permutation itself may leak through side channels.
resolves.source_text: Using the terminology of [VMKS12], we can anyway exploit a direct permutation leakage in both cases.

resolves.action_name: Use multivariate Gaussian templates (with SNR for POI selection and LDA/PCA for dimensionality reduction) to model each share, then apply Soft Analytical Side‑Channel Attacks (SASCA) to propagate beliefs through the circuit.
resolves.cause_name: Bitslice implementations leak horizontally across shares; univariate or simple divide‑and‑conquer attacks cannot fully exploit this leakage.
resolves.source_text: We propose a new methodology to evaluate masked bitslice implementations which is based on Gaussian template for information extraction and SASCA for information exploitation.

resolves.action_name: When designing a bitslice masked implementation, prefer ciphers with Sboxes that have a low number of non‑linear gates (AND) to reduce the attack surface for horizontal attacks.
resolves.cause_name: Clyde's Sbox has fewer AND gates (4) compared to AES (32), resulting in fewer leakage points and less algorithmic noise that can be averaged by horizontal attacks.
resolves.source_text: We show that bitslice ciphers with limited number of AND gates better resist the advanced (multivariate, horizontal and analytical) attacks we consider.

resolves.action_name: Instead of shuffling tuples, shuffle the shares within each operation (i.e., randomize the order in which shares are processed). This allows masking to amplify the effect of shuffling, leading to an exponential security gain.
resolves.cause_name: Shuffling tuples (i.e., randomizing the order of independent operations) only forces the adversary to guess the correct operation index, providing a security gain linear in the permutation size.
resolves.source_text: shuffling tuples only provides a security gain linear in the number of independent operations, while shuffling shares provides a gain exponential in the number of shares (amplified by masking).

resolves.action_name: Increase the number of traces, try a different bit for the leakage model, or apply windowing to focus on the leakage region.
resolves.cause_name: Insufficient trace count, or the chosen bit does not exhibit strong leakage, or the leakage is spread over time and requires windowing.
resolves.source_text: One artifact of a DPA attack is you get another strong peak that isn't the correct key (which can be a ghost peak). Solutions: Increase the number of traces recorded. Change the targeted bit (& combine solutions from multiple bits). Window the input data.

resolves.action_name: Examine the full difference traces for top candidates, not just the maximum value. Look for a location where the correct guess's difference trace shows a distinctly higher peak.
resolves.cause_name: The difference traces for incorrect guesses may have peaks in different locations, and the global maximum might not coincide with the correct leakage point.
resolves.source_text: Zoom in on the window, and you should notice there is a location where the correct peak is higher than the incorrect peaks.

resolves.action_name: Use more efficient implementations (e.g., vectorized numpy operations) or switch to more powerful attacks like CPA.
resolves.cause_name: Python loops are inefficient for processing large trace arrays and performing 256 guesses per byte across thousands of traces.
resolves.source_text: If you want to perform these attacks in practice, the Python code here isn't the most efficient! We'll look at faster options in later courses.

resolves.action_name: Subtract average trace then average by Hamming weight groups
resolves.cause_name: SBox power consumption is too small relative to noise and other operations
resolves.source_text: Instead, let's approach this from a different angle. Really, what we want here is to remove the overall 'shape' of the trace and just leave the signal from the SBox output.

resolves.action_name: Invert measurement direction (multiply trace by -1)
resolves.cause_name: Measurement shunt resistor causes voltage drop when current increases (higher current = lower measured voltage)
resolves.source_text: We can fix the slope by simply inverting the measurement direction (adding a - in front of the measurement).

resolves.action_name: Use lookup table for Hamming weight calculation
resolves.cause_name: String operations for Hamming weight calculation are computationally slow
resolves.source_text: Even better, create a lookup table (aka do the calculation for each number between 0 and 255 and stick them in an array)

resolves.action_name: Rank key guesses by absolute value of correlation coefficient
resolves.cause_name: Power consumption may be inversely proportional to Hamming weight, resulting in negative correlation slope
resolves.source_text: We're taking the absolute value of the correlation here since we only care that the relation between hamming weight and the power trace is linear, not that the slope is positive or negative.

resolves.action_name: Switch to online correlation formula for incremental updates
resolves.cause_name: Standard correlation formula requires processing entire dataset, causing inefficiency and lack of intermediate feedback
resolves.source_text: This isn't too bad for a short attack, for a much longer one (think 10k+ traces) we won't get any feedback from the attack until it's finished. Also, if we didn't capture enough traces for the attack, the entire analysis calculation needs to be repeated!

resolves.action_name: Reduce the number of samples captured to focus only on the interval containing the leakage point, speeding up analysis.
resolves.cause_name: The leakage point (SBox operation) is only a small portion of the total trace length. Processing the entire trace is inefficient.
resolves.source_text: We are normally talking absolute values, so you'll see negatives in there. This information can be useful in many ways. For example, you can probably see the first 16 spikes that make up the sbox lookup are a small portion of the total trace length. If we ever needed to rerun the attack, we could capture a much smaller number of samples and speed up analysis significantly!

resolves.action_name: Use the PGE vs. Traces plot to determine the minimum number of traces needed for successful key recovery and adjust future capture/analysis accordingly.
resolves.cause_name: The attack may succeed with fewer traces than the total captured. Using all traces for analysis is unnecessary if the key is recovered earlier.
resolves.source_text: You should see a number of lines that start off with high values, then rapidly drop off. You may notice that we broke the AES implementation without needing to use all of our traces.

resolves.action_name: Use a callback function with a defined reporting interval (e.g., every 10 traces) to get intermediate results during the CPA attack.
resolves.cause_name: Processing all traces before getting results prevents early termination and limits insight into the attack's convergence.
resolves.source_text: ChipWhisperer Analyzer actually uses the 'online' correlation calculation that we mentioned last time, meaning we can get feedback during the attack. This can be done by creating a callback function and passing it to attack.run().

resolves.action_name: Choose the reporting interval based on the need: lower values for detailed progress monitoring and plot resolution, higher values for faster overall execution.
resolves.cause_name: The choice of reporting interval involves a trade-off between performance and resolution. More frequent reporting increases overhead but provides finer-grained data for analysis.
resolves.source_text: Depending on the attack and what you want to learn from it, you may want to use higher or lower values: in general reporting less often is faster, but more frequent reporting can allow you to end a long attack early. More frequent reporting also increases the resolution of some plot data.

resolves.action_name: Set scope.trigger.triggers to 'tio1' (RX) instead of 'tio2' (TX).
resolves.cause_name: The receive (RX) trigger is under control of the target device, while the transmit (TX) trigger is subject to host-side jitter.
resolves.source_text: As discussed in the training video - this makes sense, because the receive trigger is being sent under control of the target device.

resolves.action_name: Set scope.clock.adc_src = 'clkgen_x1' to reduce ADC sampling rate.
resolves.cause_name: A slower ADC clock (clkgen_x1) provides more samples per target clock cycle, giving a larger window to capture the encryption operation when using a less precise trigger.
resolves.source_text: But by running the ADC clock at x1 the target, instead of x4, we basically get 4 times as many useful sample points.

resolves.action_name: Set scope.adc.presamples to a value (e.g., 20000) to capture data before the trigger edge.
resolves.cause_name: The encryption operation begins after the target receives the plaintext, which may occur before the RX pin's falling edge (which signals the start of the response).
resolves.source_text: Run this block - you'll see a lack of interesting activity! So use a feature called 'presample' which allows us to sample 'before' the trigger.

resolves.action_name: Change the order: call scope.arm(), then send plaintext, then read response, then call scope.capture().
resolves.cause_name: The scope.capture() function blocks waiting for the trigger, which now occurs during the UART communication. If we wait for the trigger before reading the response, the target may have already sent the response and the trigger event may have passed.
resolves.source_text: We need to change this around a little bit. Instead, we need to call scope.capture() *after* the serial data exchange happened.

resolves.action_name: Resynchronize traces using Sum of Absolute Difference (SAD) alignment.
resolves.cause_name: Traces are misaligned due to jitter, causing the leakage point to shift between traces, which reduces pointwise correlation.
resolves.source_text: As expected, the attack completely failed. ... You should see the attack succeed this time!

resolves.action_name: Select a reference trace segment that is unique, not too close to the edges, and from a stable region of the power trace.
resolves.cause_name: A poor reference (non-unique, too close to edges, or in a highly variable region) can lead to incorrect or unstable alignment.
resolves.source_text: We want it to be fairly 'unique' - we don't want something earlier or later on to also match easily. ... the reference in green would be a good spot to pick, while the reference in red would be a poor choice

resolves.action_name: Set an appropriate SAD threshold and a maximum shift limit (max_shift) to discard traces that cannot be properly aligned.
resolves.cause_name: Without a threshold, the algorithm might not find a match; without max_shift, traces shifted beyond the capture window may be incorrectly included, disrupting the attack.
resolves.source_text: max_shift, which will cause the ResyncSAD object to discard a trace if it needs to be shifted more than max_shift. ... It would be much better to simply discard this trace, rather than including it and having it disrupt our data.

resolves.action_name: Replace ResyncSAD with ResyncDTW (Dynamic Time Warp).
resolves.cause_name: Jitter during the encryption operation (multiple delays) cannot be corrected by a single global shift (SAD).
resolves.source_text: This target is inserting multiple delays during the actual encryption itself. This means that shifting traces by a single offset isn't going to be very effective.

resolves.action_name: Start with radius=1 and increase if needed for better resync.
resolves.cause_name: Higher radius gives better synchronization but at the cost of higher processing time.
resolves.source_text: Higher radii will generally give a better synchronization, but at the cost of a higher processing time. 1 is a good value to start with, but you might have to bump it a bit higher to get a good resync.

resolves.action_name: Use T-table leakage model instead of SBox output model
resolves.cause_name: T-table implementation accesses multiple bytes (sbox[a], 2*sbox[a], 3*sbox[a]) in one 32-bit lookup, so the Hamming weight of the entire 32-bit access captures more leakage.
resolves.source_text: we can see that for each T-Table lookup, the following is accessed: sbox[a], sbox[a], 2×sbox[a], 3×sbox[a] so instead of just taking the Hamming weight of the SBox, we can instead take the Hamming weight of this whole access

resolves.action_name: Use Hamming distance between the output and input of the last round as the leakage model.
resolves.cause_name: Hardware implementations combine operations and may process the last round in a single clock cycle, storing input and output in the same memory block. The last round is close to ciphertext, has AddRoundKey and SubBytes (nonlinear key addition), and no MixColumns, making it a suitable target. The reset assumption for Hamming weight may not hold, so Hamming distance is more appropriate.
resolves.source_text: Our reset assumption that allowed us to simply use the Hamming weight instead of the Hamming distance also probably won't be valid here. As such, let's use the Hamming distance between the output and the input of the last round.

resolves.action_name: Adjust the analysis interval to focus on one of the spikes.
resolves.cause_name: Multiple leakage points may be present in the trace interval, causing interference and incorrect key guesses for some bytes.
resolves.source_text: Try focusing the attack on either one of these points by adjusting `start=` and `end=` when making the `cw_container`

resolves.action_name: Use modified CPA attack with chosen plaintexts (keep 3 bytes constant, vary 1 byte per column) and attack one bit at a time
resolves.cause_name: MixColumns combines 4 bytes, making leakage depend on 2^32 combinations instead of 2^8 per byte
resolves.source_text: Instead, we can attack v' one bit at a time... taking us back to a 2^8 attack! We also don't have to worry about the ghost peaks

resolves.action_name: Take absolute value of correlation to remove constant's effect
resolves.cause_name: The constant c_a in d0 = 2v'0 + c_a only flips the correlation sign if its corresponding bit is 1
resolves.source_text: This means we can completely remove the effect of the constant by taking the absolute value of the correlation

resolves.action_name: Sum absolute correlations across all bits (8 bits) and all four MixColumn outputs (d0-d3)
resolves.cause_name: One bit of leakage has low signal-to-noise ratio
resolves.source_text: Adding in these brings us up to 32 CPA attacks... summing the absolute correlations

resolves.action_name: Use trace_slice to window the analysis to the relevant leakage region
resolves.cause_name: Noise outside the leakage window dilutes correlation
resolves.source_text: Windowing can also be very important with this attack. You can adjust the window you analyzer with trace_slice

resolves.action_name: Increase trace length to 15000 samples
resolves.cause_name: AES-256 attack requires capturing two rounds (13th and 14th), so a longer trace is needed to cover both
resolves.source_text: The normal 5000 traces we capture isn't long enough to get the rounds we care about, so we'll need to increase it (15000 should be fine).

resolves.action_name: Restrict CPA point range to (2900, 4200) for XMEGA when attacking 14th round
resolves.cause_name: The entire trace is 11000 samples, but only a portion contains the leakage for the 14th round
resolves.source_text: 11000 samples is a rather large amount to chew through, so if you want a faster attack you can use a smaller range in attack.point_range. (2900, 4200) will work for XMEGA

resolves.action_name: Restrict CPA point range to (1400, 2600) for STM32F3 (CWLite ARM) when attacking 14th round
resolves.cause_name: The entire trace is 11000 samples, but only a portion contains the leakage for the 14th round
resolves.source_text: 11000 samples is a rather large amount to chew through, so if you want a faster attack you can use a smaller range in attack.point_range. (1400, 2600) will work for the STM32F3 (CWLite ARM).

resolves.action_name: Apply ResyncSAD preprocessing to correct desynchronization
resolves.cause_name: Non-constant AES implementation (timing variability) in the XMEGA firmware
resolves.source_text: The traces for the XMEGA version of the firmware become desynced around sample 7000. This is due to a non-constant AES implementation.

resolves.action_name: Set CPA point range to (8000, 10990) for XMEGA when attacking 13th round
resolves.cause_name: The leakage for the 13th round occurs in a specific later part of the trace
resolves.source_text: attack.point_range = [8000,10990] works well for the XMEGA

resolves.action_name: Set CPA point range to (6500, 8500) for STM32F3 (CWLite ARM) when attacking 13th round
resolves.cause_name: The leakage for the 13th round occurs in a specific later part of the trace
resolves.source_text: attack.point_range = [6500,8500] works well for the STM32F3

resolves.action_name: Collect at least 5000 traces for DPA-based IV recovery on XMEGA
resolves.cause_name: The signal-to-noise ratio is lower for XMEGA, requiring more traces for a successful DPA on the IV
resolves.source_text: N=5000 #oof DPA attacks on XMEGA

resolves.action_name: Use 500 traces for DPA-based IV recovery on ARM
resolves.cause_name: The signal-to-noise ratio is higher for ARM, so fewer traces are needed
resolves.source_text: N = 500  # Number of traces [for ARM]

resolves.action_name: Correlate traces only in the sample range where signature check occurs
resolves.cause_name: The signature check occurs at a specific time in the trace, so correlating the entire trace is inefficient and noisy
resolves.source_text: corr.append(np.corrcoef(mean[18000:20000], traces[i][18000:20000])[0, 1])

resolves.action_name: Capture exactly 256 traces, one for each possible byte value
resolves.cause_name: To test each possible byte value for a signature byte, we need one trace per hypothesis
resolves.source_text: N = 256 # Number of traces [for each signature byte]

resolves.action_name: use ResyncSAD preprocessing to align traces
resolves.cause_name: timing variability in the bootloader's decryption operation
resolves.source_text: We can eliminate a lot of this jitter by using the resync SAD module

resolves.action_name: plan to run two CPA attacks: first on round 14, then on round 13
resolves.cause_name: AES256 has 14 rounds, so 13 repetitions of MixColumns indicate AES256
resolves.source_text: there's actually 13. This rules out AES128, but AES256 actually has 14 rounds!

resolves.action_name: look for XOR operations at the end of the encryption and perform a DPA attack to recover the IV
resolves.cause_name: the bootloader is using a block cipher mode (CBC) that uses an Initialization Vector (IV)
resolves.source_text: As we expected, we still get gibberish out of this - the target is definitely using AES as a stream cipher.

resolves.action_name: reset the device for each trace capture when attacking the IV
resolves.cause_name: the bootloader uses the same IV for the first block until reset
resolves.source_text: We'll need to reset the device every encryption since it only uses the IV in the first encryption.

resolves.action_name: Use CpaPartitionedEngine instead of CpaEngine for small partition sizes
resolves.cause_name: Small partition size (e.g., 256 for 8-bit target) enables faster computation with partitioned engine
resolves.source_text: The CpaPartitionedEngine takes profits of this property, and computes a Cpa more quickly than a CpaEngine would have done.

resolves.action_name: Use precomputed leakage models when available for target leakage function
resolves.cause_name: Precomputed leakage models avoid recomputation for every guess and trace, improving performance
resolves.source_text: leakage_model = HammingPrecomputedModel()

resolves.action_name: Set JULIA_NUM_THREADS to a value >1 for Jlsca incremental correlation
resolves.cause_name: Jlsca's incremental correlation algorithm benefits from parallel processing, but Julia defaults to a single thread
resolves.source_text: Jlsca's incremental correlation benefits from more threads. By default Julia only has 1 thread, but you can configure this by setting environment variable JULIA_NUM_THREADS.

resolves.action_name: Plot a few traces and check if they are well aligned.
resolves.cause_name: Initial visual inspection of a few traces is a quick sanity check for gross misalignment before committing to full analysis.
resolves.source_text: plot(samples[1:3,1:40]', linewidth=.3) ... Well aligned, should be piece of cake indeed.

resolves.action_name: Apply alignment preprocessing before CPA
resolves.cause_name: Misalignment obscures leakage patterns and reduces CPA correlation
resolves.source_text: observe the alignment is not very good

resolves.action_name: Adjust the alignment correlation threshold
resolves.cause_name: Low alignment correlation threshold includes poorly aligned traces, harming CPA
resolves.source_text: bump the corvalMin to throw away stuff that is poorly aligned

resolves.action_name: Crop traces to a window of interest after alignment
resolves.cause_name: Full trace length adds computational cost and noise from irrelevant sections
resolves.source_text: throwing away everything outside our window of interest before it goes into the attack, after alignment

resolves.action_name: Set minimum correlation threshold to discard poorly aligned traces
resolves.cause_name: Poorly aligned traces harm attack success rate
resolves.source_text: bump the corvalMin to throw away stuff that is poorly aligned

resolves.action_name: Crop trace to region of interest after alignment
resolves.cause_name: Full trace length is computationally expensive for attack phase
resolves.source_text: throwing away samples to speed up the LRA analysis (removing this pass does not affect the attack outcome)

resolves.action_name: Verify key by encrypting known plaintext and comparing with ciphertext from trace set
resolves.cause_name: Recovered key might be incorrect due to misalignment, insufficient traces, or other issues
resolves.source_text: Check the key using a plaintext-ciphertext pair from the traceset

resolves.action_name: Use CondReduce (or similar) as a post-processor in the analysis
resolves.cause_name: Automatic point-of-interest selection (CondReduce) removes irrelevant samples without manual inspection
resolves.source_text: Before computing the correlation, we perform pre-processing on the traces to automatically remove samples that are irrelevant for the analysis. Such point-of-interest selection drastically reduces the length of traces without the visual inspection of the trace graph and manual filter configuration.

resolves.action_name: Set condavg = true to use conditional leakage averaging for faster key recovery at the cost of requiring more traces
resolves.cause_name: Conditional leakage averaging can speed up key recovery time but requires more traces
resolves.source_text: conditional leakage averaging approach can speed up the key recovery time while using more traces

resolves.action_name: apply bandpass filter
resolves.cause_name: To remove noise and improve signal-to-noise ratio for CPA
resolves.source_text: Nous avons appliqué un filtre passe-bande (1-20 MHz) pour supprimer le bruit.

resolves.action_name: skip alignment step
resolves.cause_name: Stable trigger means traces are already aligned in time
resolves.source_text: Nous n'avons pas aligné les traces car le trigger était stable.

resolves.action_name: Use weight 2-3 for software implementations (smartcard, MCU). Use no filter for hardware implementations (FPGA, ASIC).
resolves.cause_name: Software implementations have clear signal; too high weight distorts signal and reduces CPA success. Hardware implementations generally do not require filtering.
resolves.source_text: 软件实现（智能卡、MCU）：权重设为2-3。硬件实现（FPGA、ASIC）：一般不需要滤波。

resolves.action_name: Perform vertical alignment using a flat non-encryption region (before encryption peaks) as reference. Subtract each trace's baseline mean.
resolves.cause_name: Different traces have different baseline levels, which can drown CPA correlation.
resolves.source_text: 纵向对齐的触发条件与 Step 4-5 无关。即使 Step 4 直接 CPA 成功，也要判断是否需要纵向对齐。

resolves.action_name: Use target S-box_out with HW model.
resolves.cause_name: Software implementations leak the Hamming weight of the S-box output.
resolves.source_text: 软件实现（智能卡、MCU）：泄露模型：Hamming Weight (HW)

resolves.action_name: Use target S-box_in_xor_prev_ct (or other HD targets) with HW model, and enable dual mode for linear HD targets.
resolves.cause_name: Hardware implementations leak Hamming distance of register transitions.
resolves.source_text: 硬件实现（FPGA、ASIC）：泄露模型：HD（Hamming Distance，汉明距离）——通过 target 的 XOR 组合表达，leakage_model 仍选 HW

resolves.action_name: Perform 4-round CPA, using target S-box_out (or other) and adjusting wave_start/wave_end for each round.
resolves.cause_name: SM4 requires 4 rounds of CPA, each recovering 4 bytes of round key, then deriving the master key.
resolves.source_text: 攻击方式：4 轮依次 CPA，每轮恢复 4 字节 round key，第 N 轮需要前 N-1 轮的 round key 作为输入

resolves.action_name: Use the recovered key (with 0 parity bits) for encryption verification; it will match the original key's encryption result.
resolves.cause_name: DES internally discards parity bits via PC-1 permutation, so CPA recovered key has 0 parity bits, which is correct.
resolves.source_text: DES密钥每个字节的最后一位是奇偶校验位。CPA恢复的密钥校验位全部为0，这是正确且预期的结果。

resolves.action_name: Observe peak position variation in several traces and set max_shift to the actual range (max_pos - min_pos).
resolves.cause_name: max_shift is too small, not covering the actual position offset range.
resolves.source_text: 如果丢弃率超过5-10%，首先检查max_shift是不是太小

resolves.action_name: Try weight 2, weight 3, and no filter.
resolves.cause_name: Over-filtering (weight too high).
resolves.source_text: 滤波过度：检查滤波权重是否过大（从小的权重做起）

resolves.action_name: Check alignment by viewing superimposed traces after alignment; ensure feature peaks are aligned.
resolves.cause_name: Poor alignment.
resolves.source_text: 对齐效果不好：检查对齐后的波形叠加图，确保特征位置已对齐

resolves.action_name: Use S-box output as attack point.
resolves.cause_name: Wrong attack point (e.g., using S-box input instead of output).
resolves.source_text: 攻击位置选错（如用了S-box输入而非输出）

resolves.action_name: Set length to 100-120, max_shift to actual offset range, threshold to 85.
resolves.cause_name: length too short, max_shift too large, threshold too low, leading to false high acceptance.
resolves.source_text: length太短+threshold太低"骗"来的接受率

resolves.action_name: Check peak position variation and set max_shift to the actual range.
resolves.cause_name: max_shift too small, so only traces with small offset are kept, which are not enough for the second half.
resolves.source_text: max_shift 太小。特征峰在不同trace之间的实际位置偏移超过了 max_shift 的范围

resolves.action_name: Do not use global maximum peak for alignment. Use mean+3σ to find the first prominent peak in the candidate encryption interval.
resolves.cause_name: The global maximum peak is often protocol/IO, not S-box leakage.
resolves.source_text: 波形最大尖峰（np.argmax）通常是 IO/协议信号，不是 S-box 泄漏位置

resolves.action_name: Even with low correlation, if high_confidence_count is ≥6/8, CPA is successful and key_search can recover master key.
resolves.cause_name: Hardware HD target naturally has low correlation, but the correct subkey may still be top-1.
resolves.source_text: DES 硬件 HD target 的信号量级和 master key 恢复

resolves.action_name: Check if the alignment interval is the correct encryption interval. Try different start positions.
resolves.cause_name: Alignment may be to the wrong interval (non-encryption peak).
resolves.source_text: 对齐质量好 ≠ 攻击会成功（指标分离原则）

resolves.action_name: Use gap_pct to decide whether to trust a byte or to improve CPA or use key_search.
resolves.cause_name: gap_pct indicates byte-level confidence: ≥15% high confidence, 10-15% gray, <10% low.
resolves.source_text: gap_pct 三段带定义：≥15% 高可信，10%-15% 灰色带，<10% 接近零信号

resolves.action_name: Perform direct CPA first. If high_confidence_count is in green band (AES≥13, DES≥6, SM4 per round≥3), skip static alignment.
resolves.cause_name: Static alignment is not always necessary and may worsen results if aligned to wrong peak.
resolves.source_text: 静态对齐不是必须步骤。判断要不要做静态对齐的流程就是 Step 4 的第一次 CPA 试探

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Two-stage SAD alignment and grouped attack for non-deterministic MixColumns
strategy_applies_to.source_text: I used a coarse SAD filter first... Then I used a secondary extremely fine SAD... I first attacked key bytes 0, 13, 10, 7 then realigned to the next mix word...

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Two-stage SAD alignment and grouped attack for non-deterministic MixColumns
strategy_applies_to.source_text: I used a coarse SAD filter first... Then I used a secondary extremely fine SAD... I first attacked key bytes 0, 13, 10, 7 then realigned to the next mix word...

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Two-stage SAD alignment and grouped attack for non-deterministic MixColumns
strategy_applies_to.source_text: I used a coarse SAD filter first... Then I used a secondary extremely fine SAD... I first attacked key bytes 0, 13, 10, 7 then realigned to the next mix word...

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Criteria for selecting an alignment pattern
strategy_applies_to.source_text: 选择模式时，需要考虑下述属性：唯一性、数据依赖性、长度、与被攻击中间结果的距离。

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Criteria for selecting an alignment pattern
strategy_applies_to.source_text: 选择模式时，需要考虑下述属性：唯一性、数据依赖性、长度、与被攻击中间结果的距离。

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: Static alignment default parameter bundle for contact smartcard AES
strategy_applies_to.source_text: 参考波形号：1，最大偏移量：400，阈值：85，点长度：100

strategy_applies_to.source_text: 参考波形号：1，最大偏移量：400，阈值：85，点长度：100

strategy_applies_to.strategy_name: EM trace filtering and alignment for DES
